title: From Monovalent Dev to Bivalent DevOps to Trivalent DevIntOps: Intelligence as the Third Continuous Loop in Software Engineering
description:
Draft. Canonical web version: https://devintops.org/v1/.

DevIntOps puts what a software system learns under a contract: what each lesson records, what it may change, how its effect is checked and how it leaves. Many agentic SDLC proposals put an AI agent into every box of the DevOps figure-eight. That can make each box faster, but it doesn't by itself carry experience from one task to the next. This paper makes learning an explicit, persistent and measured third loop next to Development and Operations: Intelligence (Understand, Predict, Orchestrate, Learn, with memory and judgment at its core), which turns outcomes such as escaped bugs, incidents, review feedback, wasted work and changes that went well into lessons that change how each stage decides. The same logical pattern applies to the engineering system and to the decisions a product makes for its users. It is a step toward self-improving software systems, with a bound: the loop aims to make later decisions better, while people keep the goals, the permissions and the scoring. A chemistry metaphor frames the shift: monovalent Dev, bivalent DevOps, trivalent DevIntOps.
